title: Self-healing offline bootstrap and egress-mirror acceptance checklist for Private/VPC
creator: Amelia Park
description: Problem statement: Customers deploying Redwood Private into highly restricted VPCs or air-gapped sites require a deterministic, auditable bootstrap and upgrade flow that recovers automatically when external egress is unavailable, and that can safely fall back to locally mirrored artifacts during upgrades. Scope: Define concrete requirements and acceptance criteria for operator bootstrap resilience, mirrored artifact validation, egress-failover behavior, and upgrade rollback triggers for Private/VPC installs. This PRD does not define implementation details for each operator; it focuses on observable contracts and testable outcomes for product and ops teams.
acceptance_criteria: Offline bootstrap: When control-plane egress is blocked, the installer/operator must succeed to a healthy state using only locally-provisioned images and artifacts within a configurable timeout (default 30m). Success is defined as: all core control-plane pods running, K8s CRDs present, and node-agent heartbeat within 120s.

Egress-mirror discovery: Operators must support two mirror discovery modes: explicit-mirror (customer-provided registry URL + credentials) and ephemeral-cache (pre-seeded artifact bundle). In both modes the operator verifies checksums and image signatures before tagging images for use.

Image provenance: All mirrored images and bundles must be signed and verifiable with embedded or customer KMS-provided keys. Installer must fail fast with an explicit error code when signature verification fails and provide remediation hints.

Upgrade canary and automatic rollback: For upgrades performed in an air-gapped environment, a single-node canary (or single-pod canary depending on topology) must be applied first. If SLO health checks (startup probes, API readiness, telemetry heartbeats) do not converge within 10 minutes, operator automatically rolls back to previous controller revision and produces an audit record with reason and metrics snapshot.

Egress-exception policy: If an operator requires outbound calls for telemetry/validation, those calls must be configurable via an explicit egress whitelist. By default, the product ships with zero required egress; any external endpoints must be optional and non-blocking to core control-plane functionality.

Deterministic timeouts and observability: All bootstrap and upgrade phases emit structured events to the operator status and to the local audit log including phase start, phase end, duration, success/failure, and error codes. These events must be queryable by Console and exported to customer SIEM via existing audit hooks.

Artifact distribution fallback: If a staged upgrade detects that primary mirror is unreachable, the operator must attempt configured fallback mirrors in order and then revert to local bundle. Failure modes must be surfaced as distinct error codes and metrics.

KMS rotation in air-gapped mode: Key rotation operations may require operator-led offline wrapping. Acceptance requires tooling to rotate keys using a local HSM or provided offline-wrapping file and to validate rotated keys before committing to cluster state.

Upgrade gating for critical workloads: Customers may mark specific namespaces/workloads as "must-not-disrupt". The operator must skip disruptive operations for these namespaces during staged upgrades and include them in preflight validation reports.

Test harness: A repeatable test harness (CI job / local script) must exist that simulates: no-egress bootstrap, mirror-signature mismatch, canary failure and automatic rollback, and mirror failover. Tests must produce deterministic pass/fail and logs for postmortem review.

Compliance artifacts: The operator must emit an upgrade artifact bundle containing pre-upgrade snapshot (images + manifest checksums), upgrade plan, and post-upgrade verification report that customers can archive for audits.
Operator configurability: All timeouts, retry counts, mirror lists, and canary sizing must be configurable via a single operatorConfig CRD with clear default values and validation schema.

Manual override path: Provide documented manual intervention steps that allow operators to: promote a local bundle to canonical mirror, force-rollback a failed upgrade, and run forensic verification of signatures and checksums without destroying cluster state.
Security review: Any flow that enables offline key material or local signing must pass a security checklist and be surfaced as a flag that requires explicit customer acknowledgement before use.

Customer telemetry opt-in: By default, product behavior must not exfiltrate customer telemetry in air-gapped installs. Any telemetry collection requires an explicit opt-in switch and documentation of what is sent and how to disable it.

Performance constraint: In typical medium-sized clusters (20 worker nodes, median request sizes), offline bootstrap using a pre-seeded bundle should complete within 20 minutes in 90th percentile conditions on standard on-prem hypervisors.

Rollback verification: After an automatic rollback, the operator must verify cluster control-plane is responsive and emit an actionable incident summary including which resources were reverted and why.

User-facing errors: All user-facing errors for offline/bootstrap/upgrade flows must include a unique machine-readable error code, a short human-friendly reason, and next-step remediation in the message.
Auditability and retention: Audit logs for bootstrap and upgrade flows must be retained for a configurable retention period (default 90 days) and be exportable in JSON and plain-text formats.

Backward compatibility: New operator config fields must provide defaults that maintain compatibility with previously deployed clusters (no-change by default). Any change that requires manual migration must be accompanied by a documented migration job.
Operator health gateway: A single health endpoint must reflect aggregated bootstrap/upgrade health and map to Console readiness indicators and alerting rules.
Acceptance sign-off: PM + Eng + Security must sign acceptance before GA for customers with offline requirements.
Documentation: Provide a step-by-step runbook for each acceptance criterion above and a quick-start checklist that customers can run to validate their environment prior to install/upgrade.
